abstract.p: An angularly adjustable side view mirror (11) mounted upon a first vehicle (10) is normally positioned to display to a driver reflections of the area (23) at the side and rear of the vehicle. The mirror is temporarily angularly adjusted by a motor, out of its normal position into a temporary position which displays to the driver a following vehicle (40) that is momentarily located in the first vehicle's side blind spot area (25). The motor angularly turns the mirror a predetermined amount from its preset normal position to its pre-determined temporary position and then back to its normal position in response to signals from a detector. The detector activates the motor to move and hold the mirror in the temporary blind spot area viewing position while the vehicle is located therein.

L'invention concerne un rétroviseur latéral à angle réglable (11) monté sur le côté d'un véhicule (10) qui est disposé normalement de façon que le conducteur puisse visualiser la zone (23) située sur le côté et l'arrière du véhicule. L'angle du rétroviseur est réglé par un moteur et le rétroviseur quitte sa position normale pour prendre une position qui permet au conducteur de visualiser un véhicule le suivant (40), provisoirement situé dans la première zone d'angle mort (25) du véhicule. Sous l'effet de signaux émis par un détecteur, le moteur modifie la position du rétroviseur selon un angle prédéterminé par rapport à sa position normale, de façon à placer le rétroviseur dans une position provisoire prédéterminée et à le replacer ensuite dans sa position initiale. Le détecteur actionne le moteur afin de déplacer et de maintenir le rétroviseur dans la position de visualisation de la zone d'angle mort provisoire tant que le véhicule suivant s'y trouve.

description.p: VEHICLE BLIND SPOT MIRROR

This invention relates to a side view automotive vehicle mirror which will automatically adjust its position to display a following vehicle located in the "blind spot" zone of a leading vehicle and then automatically return, to its normal side-rear viewing position when the "blind spot" zone is clear.
BACKGROUND OF INVENTION

Automotive vehicles, such as passenger cars and trucks, conventionally have side view mirrors mounted on the sides of the vehicles to display to the driver images of the areas behind and to the sides of the vehicle. A conventional side view mirror comprises a support housing withm which an adjustable angle mirror is mounted. The housing is connected to the vehicle in various known manners. The angularity of such mirrors can be adjusted by the vehicle dπver either remotely from the driver's position behind the steeπng wheel of the vehicle, or directly by hand pressure upon the mirror to move it within the housing.

Typically, the dπver of a vehicle adjusts the angularity of the mirror so that the dπver can view a reflected image of the corresponding side and rear area of the vehicle Since the driver's position in a vehicle may vary because the dπver may adjust the position of the vehicle seat, a mechanism for angularly adjusting the mirror is necessary in order to best display the reflected image desired by the dπver.

Conventional, side view mirrors display a narrow angle and far distant side and rear area relative to the vehicle. Thus, there is normally a short distance area along the side of the vehicle which is commonly referred to as the "blind spot" zone or area which is not ordinarily visible to the dπver. In those instances where a following vehicle enters the blind spot area, the dπver of the leading vehicle may not be aware of that condition. Because the following vehicle is not readily visible to the driver of the leading vehicle, the dπver of the leading vehicle may inadvertently steer into the adjacent lane where the following vehicle is located or may veer towards the following vehicle a sufficient distance to collide with the following
vehicle Thus, accidents, involving collisions between a leading vehicle and a following vehicle located in the blind spot zone of the leading vehicle are common. At times, where the driver of the following vehicle was sufficiently alert, the following vehicle may have swerved away from the leading vehicle. That could have caused the following vehicle to run off the road or to collide with another vehicle located on the opposite side of the following vehicle.

In the case of large trucks, frequently a separate, short range, wide angle, "blind spot" zone viewing mirror is mounted below or adjacent the normal side view mirror. Thus, the driver, has two mirrors to monitor in order to obtain both the normal side-rear view and a view of the vehicle's blind spot zone. However, that can be distracting to the dπver Although separate "blind spot" or wide angle mirrors have been proposed for automobiles, the required sizes or size limitations on side view mirrors, in general, make these dual mirrors unpopular.

Thus, it would be desirable to have a dual view, side view minor available for automotive vehicles, particularly passenger automobiles and other small size vehicles, which normally displays a normal side-rear image but which, when appropriate, will temporarily display a view of the blind spot zone to the vehicle dπver. The invention herein is concerned with providing such a dual mirror which normally reflects the conventional narrow and long range side and rear view for a vehicle driver but, which will sense the presence of a following vehicle m the blind spot zone of a leading vehicle, and thereafter, will automatically adjust the angle of the mirror to momentarily display the presence of a following vehicle. When the following vehicle is no longer in the blind spot zone, the side view mirror will automatically return to its normal position.
SUMMARY OF INVENTION

This invention is concerned with a dual automotive side view mirror which normally displays a reflection of the side and rear areas relative to an automotive vehicle, but which will momentarily focus upon the blind spot zone when a following vehicle enters and is in that zone.

This invention contemplates providing a mirror assembly, with an appropriate detector and sensor system, which can be adjusted by the vehicle driver for ordinary side viewing during dnvmg. However, it also can be pre-set to focus on the blind spot zone automatically when the detector senses a vehicle in that zone. Once the following vehicle leaves that zone the system reverts back to its earlier, ordinary dnvmg position. To accomplish this, a suitable servo-motor is provided which adjusts the angularity of the mirror to enable the vehicle driver to pre-set the normal driving position of the mirror and to pre-set the temporary or blind spot focus position so that the motor automatically positions the mirror m one or the other of the pre-set positions. The pre-set positions are likely to vary for different drivers, depending upon the location of the dπver relative to the side view mirror and the normal viewing angles of the dπver. These positions may depend on the height of the driver or the position of the dπver' s eyes relative to the vehicle side view mirrors. Thus, the system requires adjustability for each particular dπver.

An object of this invention is to provide a simplified system by which a side view mirror can be pre-set into a normal viewing position relative to a particular driver and, in addition, can be pre-set into a viewing position which reflects the blind spot of the vehicle. The system includes sensing signals or beams which will detect a vehicle in the blind spot and cause the mirror to automatically move to a position that displays the blind spot area and later return the minor to its normal dπving position.

Another object of this invention is to provide a system which can be added as a modification to a presently existing minor control system or which can be separately made as an aftermarket or add-on system to control a minor assembly mounted on a vehicle.
Yet another object of this invention is to provide a system which may be sufficiently versatile so as to use different kinds of sensing signals, such as microwave, laser, ultrasonic, air pressure or the like, depending upon which may be most economical and commercially effective for a particular installation.
These and other objects and advantages of this invention will become apparent upon reading the following description, of which the attached drawings form a part.
DESCRIPTION OF DRAWINGS
Fig. 1 schematically illustrates a plan view of an automobile and the side and rear areas that are viewed in a typical side view minor.

Fig. 2 is a schematic, plan view of a leading vehicle and a following vehicle located m the blind spot zone or area of the leading vehicle and, further, schematically illustrates the emission and the return of sensing signals that detect the presence of the following vehicle m the blind spot zone.
Fig. 3 is a schematic, perspective view of a conventional minor and housing with a signal emitter and receiver on the housing.
Fig. 4 is a schematic, elevational view showing a minor and housing and a servomotor anangement for adjusting the angle of the minor.

Fig. 5 schematically shows adjusting the angles of the minor for normally viewing either the area located to the side and rear of the vehicle or alternatively viewing the blind spot zone of the vehicle.
Fig. 6 illustrates a plan, schematic illustration of a modification having the detection system mounted on the rear side of a vehicle rather than directly upon the minor housing

Fig. 7 is a plan, schematic view, illustrating another modification having an air pressure sensitive detector for providing the signal that a following vehicle is located in the bind spot zone of a lead vehicle.

Fig. 8 is a schematic circuit diagram generally showing the circuit components which form a typical electronic circuit for accomplishing the automatic control of the minor. Fig. 9 is a schematic, logic diagram illustrating the steps in the start-up of the minor control system.
DETAILED DESCRIPTION

Fig. 1 schematically illustrates an automobile 10 having a πght side minor assembly 11 and a left side minor assembly 12 mounted on the sides of the vehicle body. The minor assemblies, m general, compπse a conventional minor housing 13 which may be of different shapes and sizes. The housing supports an adjustable angle minor 14. The housing may be connected to the automobile by a connection arm or part 15 (see Fig. 3). The particular size and shape of the minor, its support housing, and the manner by which it is attached to the vehicle may vary considerably from vehicle to vehicle and forms no part of this invention.

Fig. 1 schematically shows a dπver 20 seated upon a conventional adjustable height and position front seat 21 in the vehicle. A dotted line 22 schematically shows the line of sight of the dπver to the πght side minor 11. In viewing the minor, the dπver would have a normal, view of the adjacent side area and the long distance rear area 23 relative to the vehicle. However, the dπver would not have a view of the blind spot zone or area 25 which is laterally further away from the side of the vehicle. Thus, the purpose of the invention described herein is to provide the dπver with a view of the blind spot area only when needed.

The invention is descπbed m connection with the πght side view minor 11. However, a similar construction and system is intended for the left side minor 12, if desired. Thus, although this descπption is limited to the right side minor, it equally applies to the left side minor of the vehicle.

As schematically illustrated in Fig. 4, the minor 14 is attached to a spindle 28 which is rotatably mounted withm the housing 13. The particular manner of mounting the minor is conventional. Since it may vary considerably for different model vehicles and is not part of this invention, the mounting is shown schematically rather than in detail. Those skilled in the art would be able to select the particular mounting that is appropriate for the particular minor assembly desired.

The spindle 28 is connected to a suitable gear 29 or pulley which, in turn, is connected by a gear or by an endless belt 30 to an output gear or pulley 31 of an electrical
servo-motor 32 that is energized from the battery of the vehicle. Such motor dπve systems are known for vehicles which are equipped to automatically adjust the normal angular positions of the side view minors to a pre-set position when a particular dπver enters the vehicle. In those systems, when the driver enters the vehicle and is seated, a signal indicates the presence of that particular dπver. That automatically causes the minor to turn to or adjust to a pre-set position for normal rear-side view purposes.

As mentioned above, the present system initially detects the presence of a following vehicle m the blind spot zone Then through an appropriate electronic or electrical control circuit, the system automatically causes the minor to adjust to an angle that permits the dπver to view the following vehicle while it is m the blind spot zone. After that, the detector signals the absence of the following vehicle from the blind spot zone and the minor automatically is returned by the servo-motor to the original, normal side view position. Fig. 8 schematically illustrates a circuit 35 which operates for that purpose.

Fig. 3 and 4 schematically show a sensor signal beam emitter 36 and a signal receiver 37 that are mounted on the housing 13. Since the housing does not move relative to the vehicle, the sensor emits a sensing signal beam 38 which overlaps a relatively short zone or area along the side of the vehicle The beam dissipates after passing through the blind spot zone. If the beam contacts a following vehicle 40 in the blind spot zone, a reflected beam 39 returns to the receiver 37 to activate the circuit 35 which will re-position the minor for focusing on the blind spot zone.

Fig. 6 schematically illustrates a modification in which a detector sensor 43 and receiver are mounted on the side of the vehicle body 45, such as in the trunk or over the trunk lid of the vehicle rather than in the minor housing. In that case, the sensor emits an outwardly, transversely directed, signal beam 46 which, if it strikes a vehicle 48 m the blind spot zone, results m a reflected return beam 47 directed to the receiver 44. Various types of commercially available sensors with emitters and receivers can be selected by those skilled in the art for use for the purpose intended here.
Fig. 7 schematically illustrates another modification in which the detector 50 may be in the form of an air pressure sensitive sensor which will sense changes in air pressure (schematically indicated by wavy lines 51) due to the air flow (schematically indicated by anows 51) between the leading vehicle 53 and the adjacent following vehicle 54 that is located in the blind spot zone. The pressure change between normal air pressure and the air pressure when the vehicles overlap acts as an input signal to the detection circuit. Sensitive air pressure sensing devices are commercially available and one skilled m the art would be able to select an appropπate one for this purpose.

Fig. 8 schematically illustrates an electronic control circuit. Fig. 9 illustrates the logic or steps for the dπver to pre-set the circuit so that the minor can be either in the normal side view position or in the pre-determmed blind spot view position.

The minor control circuit illustrated in Fig. 8 utilizes a microwave signal for detecting a vehicle located m the blind spot of a leading vehicle. The circuit has an emitter or antenna which transmits a microwave beam or signal from a transmitter If the beam, which is set for a short distance, does not detect an object in the blind spot zone, nothing further happens. However, when the beam is reflected back from a vehicle in the blind spot zone, the reflected beam is picked up by a receiver or antenna and transmitted to an amplifier. At that point, the amplifier receives an analog signal which it transmits to a threshold circuit which compares the signal that is received to a reference level (schematically indicated) If the received signal is at a sufficient threshold level, the circuit transmits the signal, which is converted into a digital signal, to a microcontroller. That, in turn, signals the servo-motor driver 55 which actuates the motor 32 to turn the minor 14. The servo-motor dπver determines and sends back to the microcontroller data locating the cunent minor position before actuating the motor. In addition, the microcontroller receives from a memory circuit data about the pre-set normal position or positions A and B, if there are more than one, of the particular driver or dπvers as well as data concerning the pre-set blind spot setting or settings C and D of the particular dπver. These pre-set positions are determined by the driver. In
addition, variable position information concerning the cunent position of the minor and the desired position are supplied to the microcontroller.

In essence, the threshold circuit answers the question as to whether there is or is not a vehicle in the blind spot zone. If there is not, the remainder of the circuit is dormant. If there is, the circuit is actuated to re-set the position of the minor as indicated.

The sensing signal that is emitted is preferably a microwave signal, refened to as a radar signal. However, other detection signals and known detection techniques can be used depending upon the cost, commercial availability of components and the like. Thus, the detection signal could be m the form of an ultrasonic beam, or infrared signals or a laser beam or sonar type of sound wave or other known signaling systems. The schematic circuit diagram illustrated in Fig. 8 is intended to refer to each of these various types of signals Moreover, as mentioned above, the circuit could be used with commercially available minor adjustment systems which automatically adjust the minor to the pre-set viewing positions for a particular dπver. In those systems, the circuit and parts needed to automatically move the minor to or from viewing the blind spot zone and the initial normal positions can be added.

An alarm device, for example, in the form of an LED light 60 connected to the microcontroller, can be positioned on, or mounted within the dash board, of the vehicle m front of the dπver. The light can be actuated to visually alert the dπver to the presence of a vehicle in the blind spot. In addition, or alternatively, a conventional sound producing device (not illustrated) can be connected to the microcontroller to audibly alert the driver.

Fig. 9 schematically illustrates the steps m pre-settmg the system for use. At the start the driver re-sets the minor into the desired blind spot viewing position which is registered in the memory. Then, the dπver determines whether the blind spot is occupied. If it is not occupied, the minor is pre-set into the desired position. If that position, is determined to be the cunent position of the minor, no further act by the dπver is required.

If the blind spot is occupied, the blind spot position is loaded into the desired position for the particular driver and the system determines whether the cunent position equals that
blind spot desired position. If not, the minor is moved to the desired position. Now, the minor should have a normal position for the particular driver and a blind spot viewing position for that same particular driver. The normal and blind spot viewing positions may vary from one dπver to another. Also the positions may vary if a particular dπver moves the vehicle seat either rearwardly or forwardly or up and down. Consequently, the driver may have to re-set the normal and blind spot viewing positions from time to time.

This invention may be further developed within the scope of the following claims. Therefore, it is desired that the foregoing descπption be merely descπptive of an operative embodiment of this invention and not in a stπctly limiting sense. Having fully descπbed at least one operative embodiment of this invention, I NOW CLAIM;

claim.claim-text: 1. A vehicle blind spot viewing minor compnsmg: a minor turnably mounted within a support housing formed for attachment to a side of a first vehicle, with said minor being angularly adjustable by the vehicle driver into a normal viewing position for normally displaying to the vehicle dπver reflections of the area located rearwardly and to the side of the first vehicle; a motor connected to the minor for turning and angularly adjusting the minor so as to change the angularity of the minor relative to the dπver to a temporary viewing position for reflecting an image of the blind spot area of the first vehicle; a detector system mounted on the vehicle and including a sensor which senses the momentary presence of a following vehicle m the side blind spot area of the first vehicle; said detector system emitting a first motor actuating signal upon sensing said following vehicle m the blind spot area for causing the motor to angularly turn the minor from its normal viewing position to said temporary viewing position which displays to the driver a reflection of the vehicle occupying the blind spot; and said detector system emitting a second motor activating signal to the motor to cause the motor to angularly return the minor to its normal viewing position after the detector senses that the following vehicle is no longer in the blind spot of the first vehicle.

2. A vehicle blind spot viewing minor as set forth in claim 1 and including said detector system sensor comprising a sensing signal emitter and a sensing signal receiver for emitting a sensing beam and receiving a return reflection of the emitted sensing beam with said sensing beam being focused into the blind spot area of the first vehicle for contacting a following vehicle located in that blind spot area and reflecting the sensing beam back to the receiver and, in the absence of a vehicle in the blind spot, said sensing beam dissipating beyond said predetermined blind spot area.

3. A vehicle blind spot viewing minor as set forth in claim 2, and said signal beam being selected from one of an infrared light beam, an ultra-sonic type beam, a sonar- type beam, a radar type beam or a laser beam or the like types of conventional article sensing signals, which signal beam is substantially continuously directed into the side blind spot area of the first vehicle.

4. A vehicle blind spot viewing minor as set forth in claim 3, and said minor being operable by the vehicle dπver to turn the minor into a normal, rear viewing position and, alternatively, into a blind spot area viewing position; and said detector including a memory device for establishing each such position, and said detection system including a control for said motor to cause the motor to automatically return to the temporary or normal positions from the opposite position when signaled by a detection signal indicating the presence or absence of the following vehicle from the blind spot area.

5. A vehicle blind spot viewing minor as set forth in claim 4, including said sensor being mounted upon a side portion of the body of the first vehicle and directing its emitted detection signal generally transversely outwardly of the first vehicle towards a following vehicle which is at least partially along side of the first vehicle in the blind spot of the first vehicle.

6. A vehicle blind spot viewing minor as set forth in claim 4, and including said sensor being mounted in the minor support housing and normally directing its signal rearwardly along the side of the first vehicle into the blind spot of the first vehicle and detecting forwardly directed reflections of said detecting signal received from a vehicle in the area of the blind spot of the first vehicle.

7. A vehicle blind spot viewing minor as set forth in claim 4, and including said sensor having an air pressure measuπng device included therein for sensing changes in air pressure along the side of the first vehicle at the blind spot area and, thereby, detecting the presence of a following vehicle in the blind spot of the first vehicle by measuring predetermined changes m the air pressure between the two vehicles.

8. A vehicle blind spot viewing minor as set forth in claim 4, and including a driver alarm device located in the cabin of the first vehicle, with said alarm device displaying an alarm signal to the driver when the detector system senses a following vehicle m the blind spot of the first vehicle.

9. A side view minor for a vehicle having a minor moveably mounted upon a housing for angular adjustment by the vehicle dπver for viewing the side rear area of a vehicle, with said minor being self-adjustable temporarily into a position which displays to the dπver a following vehicle which is momentaπly in the blind spot area of the first vehicle, comprising; a detector system which includes a sensor which emits a sensor signal beam rearwardly along the side of the vehicle and a receiver which detects reflections of that signal beam bounced off a following vehicle which is momentarily m the blind spot area of the first vehicle and which actuates a motor operatively connected to the minor for turning the minor to an angle which displays a reflection of the following vehicle to the dπver; said detection system including a memory device which remembers the initial viewing position of the minor and the angular position m which the minor reflects the following vehicle located m the blind spot and which limits the movement of the minor to such positions when turned by the motor; whereby the dπver of the vehicle may pre-set the normal position of the minor for normal side and rear view visibility and may pre-set the temporary position of the minor for displaying a following vehicle in the blind spot when detected by the sensor; with said sensor signal beam being of an intensity to dissipate beyond the vehicle blind spot area.

10. A minor as defined in claim 9 and including said sensor being positioned on a minor housing and substantially continuously emitting a detection signal beam focused into the side blind spot zone of the first vehicle notwithstanding changes m the positions of the minor
